title: Cheese on Toast
subtitle: Grilled cheddar on thick white bread with worcestershire and mustard
excerpt: Cheese on toast is two thick slices of bread grilled until the cheddar bubbles and colours slightly at the edges. Worcestershire sauce and a scrape of mustard underneath the cheese give it the savoury bite that separates it from plain melted cheese. Ready in eight minutes from cold.
sourceNotes: Cheese on toast has been a British kitchen standby for well over a century. Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), Project Gutenberg #10136, includes toasted cheese as a standard savoury. The worcestershire-and-mustard combination is the standard British home version, distinct from the richer béchamel base of Welsh rarebit.

content.text: Cheese on toast is white bread toasted on one side, then loaded with grated cheddar and finished under a hot grill until the cheese bubbles. Worcestershire sauce and a thin scrape of English mustard underneath give it a proper savoury edge. It is the quickest hot snack in the British kitchen and requires no skill beyond watching the grill.

Heat the grill to its highest setting and place the shelf about 10 cm below the element. Toast the bread on both sides until firm and just golden. Take it one step short of fully done; it will go back under the grill after topping.
Spread a thin layer of {{english-mustard}} across the toasted side of each slice. Shake a few drops of {{worcestershire-sauce}} over the mustard.

Pile {{cheddar}} of grated cheddar evenly over both slices, pressing it down lightly so it covers to the edges. Return to the grill and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, watching closely, until the cheese has melted, is bubbling, and has taken a little colour at the edges. Do not leave it unattended; cheese under a hot grill goes from melted to scorched quickly.
Grind a little black pepper over the top if you like. Eat straight from the grill tray while the cheese is still molten.

items.symptom: The cheese slides off the bread
items.cause: The bread was not toasted firmly enough before topping. Soft bread cannot support the cheese weight as it melts.
items.fix: Toast the bread properly before adding the topping. The cheese anchors better to a firm, slightly rough surface.

items.symptom: The cheese is not properly melted before the top browns
items.cause: The cheese was piled too thickly, or the grill shelf was too far from the element.
items.fix: Use a coarse grate rather than thick slices, and move the shelf higher to reduce the distance to the heat.

items.symptom: The bread burns underneath before the cheese melts
items.cause: The bread was not pre-toasted, so the grill had to do two jobs at once.
items.fix: Always toast the bread fully on both sides before adding the cheese. The grill's only job is then to melt the topping.

items.cause: Too mild a cheddar, or the mustard and worcestershire were skipped.
items.fix: Use a mature or extra-mature cheddar for good flavour. The mustard and worcestershire are not optional; they are what makes it taste properly savoury.

content.text: Cheese on toast and Welsh rarebit are closely related but not the same thing. Welsh rarebit uses a cooked béchamel-and-beer sauce spread over the bread; cheese on toast uses raw grated cheese with condiments. The simpler version is what most British households reach for on a weeknight: no sauce to make, no pan to wash, two minutes of active attention. It pairs with a cup of tea in the afternoon or a bowl of tinned tomato soup at lunch.
